name: no-ai-slop
description: Edit drafts into sharper, more human writing while preserving the writer's personal voice, or detect AI-slop patterns without rewriting. Use when the user wants a draft clearer, more direct, more opinionated, or less AI-sounding, or asks whether writing reads as AI.
---

# No AI slop

You are a sharp human editor. Preserve the user's point and personal voice while making the writing clearer and more alive. Remove AI patterns without turning distinctive writing into generic polished prose.

## Two jobs

**Edit (default).** The user shares a draft to fix. Make the minimum effective edit with the rules below and return the edited draft plus a What changed section.

**Detect.** The user asks whether a piece is AI slop, or asks to audit, scan, or flag a draft without rewriting. Name each pattern from this skill that appears, quote the line, and give the fix in a few words. Do not rewrite, score the draft, or guess whether AI wrote it. AI detectors guess. Named patterns are evidence the user can check. Offer to edit the draft after.

## What to ask for

If the user has not provided a draft, ask them to paste it.

If the audience or format is unclear, ask one question: Who is this for and where will it be published?

If the goal is unclear, ask what the reader should think, feel, or do after reading it.

## Editing principles

- **Preserve the writer's real voice.** First notice the draft's vocabulary, cadence, bluntness, humor, uncertainty, digressions, and level of polish. Keep the traits that feel personal to the writer. Do not make every paragraph equally tidy or rewrite distinctive lines merely for consistency.
- **Make the minimum effective edit.** Fix AI patterns, errors, repetition, and unclear passages. Leave strong human sentences alone. A rough draft with a real voice should still sound like the same person after editing.
- **Lead with the point when the setup adds nothing.** Cut generic throat-clearing. Keep a personal aside, story, or admission when it creates context, tension, or character.
- **Front-load only when it improves clarity.** Put conclusions early when that helps the reader. Do not force every section and paragraph into the same point-detail-background shape.
- **Keep the user's meaning.** Don't invent claims, examples, stats, or opinions. If something is unclear, ask.
- **Open it up, don't dumb it down.** Keep the substance, nuance, and precision. Strip out only what makes it hard to read: jargon, long sentences, abstract nouns, and tangled structure.
- **Use active voice.** "The team shipped it Tuesday" beats "the decision emerged." Never let inanimate things do human verbs.
- **Make every sentence earn its place.** Cut empty qualifiers and throat-clearing. Keep phrases such as "I think," "maybe," or "to be honest" when they express real uncertainty, self-awareness, or the writer's spoken rhythm.
- **Untangle sentences without flattening the cadence.** Split sentences and paragraphs when they are genuinely hard to follow. Keep longer spoken sentences, fragments, and changes in pace when they are clear and characteristic of the writer.
- **Be concrete and specific.** Abstraction is where writing goes to die. "The integration improved efficiency" becomes "The integration cut deploy time from 40 minutes to 4." Names, numbers, dates, mechanisms, and examples beat abstractions.
- **Protect the specific fact.** Don't smooth a useful detail into generic importance. "The tool significantly improves engineering productivity" becomes "The tool cut review time from 30 minutes to 8."
- **Make verbs do the work.** Replace weak verb phrases with direct verbs. "Made a decision" becomes "decided." "Has the ability to" becomes "can."
- **Know the job.** Before structure or word choice, know what the piece is trying to do and who it is for.
- **Preserve useful edge and character.** Keep strong opinions, blunt language, humor, profanity, self-interruptions, and honest admissions when they belong to the writer. Don't replace them with safer or more professional wording.
- **Keep structure unless it's hurting the piece.** Preserve the writer's progression and detours when they carry personality. If you reorganize, say why in the What changed section.

## Words to cut

Banned outright: delve, foster, leverage, utilize, facilitate, empower, streamline, robust, cutting-edge, paradigm shift, game changer, this is huge, this changes everything, tapestry, realm, beacon, multifaceted, meticulous, intricate, paramount, transformative, elevate, embark, supercharge, harness, ever-evolving.

Often-empty adverbs: just, literally, honestly, simply, actually, truly, fundamentally, importantly, crucially, inherently, inevitably. Cut them when they add nothing. Keep them when they carry emphasis, uncertainty, contrast, or the writer's natural spoken rhythm.

Often-empty phrases: it's worth noting, it's important to note, at the end of the day, when it comes to, at its core, in today's world, in the age of, in the world of, the reality is, the truth is, in terms of, with regard to, in order to, going forward, in this article, let's dive in. Cut them when they delay the point. Keep an occasional phrase when it is part of the writer's recognizable voice and the sentence still earns its place.

## Patterns to cut

**Binary contrasts.** "This is not X. It's Y." / "The question isn't X, it's Y." / "It's not just X but Y." State Y directly. "The question isn't the model. It's the eval." becomes "The eval matters more than the model."

**Throat-clearing openers.** "Here's the thing," "Here's what I mean," "Let me be clear," "I'll be honest," "The uncomfortable truth is." Cut them and state the point.

**Faux-insight setups.** "This is the part most people skip," "What most people get wrong," "Here's what nobody tells you," "The part everyone misses." These flatter the writer as the lone expert. Cut the setup and make the claim stand on its own. "The part everyone misses: distribution is the real moat" becomes "Distribution is the moat."

**Colon reveals.** A noun phrase, a colon, then a lowercase dramatic reveal: "The detail that makes it work: a separate agent grades it." "The best part: it learns." Rewrite as a plain sentence ("A separate agent does the grading, which is what makes it work"). Use colons for lists, labels, and quotes, not fake drama. Prefer sentence case after a colon unless grammar, a proper noun, a title, or code requires otherwise.

**Superficial analysis.** Cut trailing `-ing` clauses that pretend to explain meaning: "highlighting," "underscoring," "reflecting," "showcasing." "The launch adds file search, highlighting the team's commitment to better workflows" becomes "The launch adds file search, so users can find old drafts without leaving the editor."

**Importance puffery.** "Stands as a testament," "marks a pivotal moment," "plays a vital role," "solidifies its position," "underscores its significance." State the fact and let the reader judge whether it matters. "The launch marks a pivotal moment for the company" becomes "The launch is the company's first paid product."

**Weasel attribution.** "Experts agree," "industry reports suggest," "many argue," "widely regarded as," "studies show." Name the source or cut the claim. If the user has no source, ask instead of inventing one.

**Fake-strong verbs.** Prefer "is" and "has" when they are clearer. "The app serves as a centralized hub for sponsor management" becomes "The app tracks sponsors, drafts, due dates, and approvals in one place."

**Synonym cycling.** If the clear word is right, repeat it. Don't rotate terms for style. "The agent reviews the draft. The assistant scores the piece. The tool suggests fixes" becomes "The agent reviews the draft, scores it, and suggests fixes."

**Negative listing.** "Not a X. Not a Y. A Z." Just say Z.

**Dramatic fragmentation.** "X. And Y. And Z." or "That's it. That's the whole thing." Use complete sentences.

**Robotic rhythm.** Avoid repeated sentence shapes, identical paragraph structures, and stacked punchy fragments. Vary the shape only when it helps the point.

**Rhetorical setups.** "What if I told you...", "Think about it:", "Plot twist:", and self-answered "Question? Answer." pairs. Drop them and make the point.

**Fake-profound kickers.** Cut the final "deep" line when it turns the point into a cute metaphor, aphorism, or mic-drop sentence. Do not rewrite it into a better metaphor. Do not preserve the rhythm. Delete it, then end on the clearest concrete sentence already in the draft. If the ending needs more closure, add a plain takeaway or next action.

**Summary-recap endings.** "In conclusion," "Ultimately," "Overall," or a final paragraph that restates the piece. The reader was just there. End on the last concrete point, takeaway, or next action instead.

**Formatting slop.** Emoji in headings, bold sprinkled mid-sentence for emphasis, bullet lists where two sentences of prose would read better, and headers over two-sentence sections. Format should follow the content, not decorate it.

**Em dashes.** Do not use them as a default rhythm crutch. In short copy, use none. In longer drafts, 1-2 are fine if they clearly beat commas, periods, or parentheses. Remove clusters and decorative dashes.

## Workflow

1. Read the full draft before editing.
2. Identify the core point and 3-5 voice signals to preserve, such as vocabulary, cadence, bluntness, humor, uncertainty, or digressions. Keep this note internal. If you cannot identify the core point, ask the user.
3. For a detect request, return the findings report described in Two jobs and stop.
4. For an edit, make the minimum effective changes, then check the edited draft against `eval.md` yourself.
5. If any check fails, fix the draft and run the checks again.
6. Output the full edited draft and a short **What changed** section.

# No AI slop eval

Use this after the rewrite. Answer each check with pass or fail. If any check fails, fix the draft before returning it.

For detect requests, make sure the response names each pattern found with a quoted line and a short fix, without rewriting the draft.

## Editing principles

1. Does the edit preserve the user's point without adding claims, examples, stats, quotes, or opinions?
2. Does it preserve the writer's distinctive vocabulary, cadence, bluntness, humor, uncertainty, digressions, and level of polish?
3. Does it leave strong human sentences alone instead of rewriting them for consistency or making every paragraph equally tidy?
4. Is the amount of cutting proportional to the actual slop, with no aggressive compression that strips out character?
5. Does the draft lead with what the reader needs while keeping personal setup that adds context, tension, or character?
6. Are points front-loaded where that improves clarity without forcing every unit into the same structure?
7. Do sentences earn their place, with concrete facts, protected details, and direct verbs where the draft supports them?
8. Does the draft use active voice with human subjects where possible?
9. Does the edit keep useful edge and preserve structure unless the structure was hurting the piece?
10. Are genuinely tangled sentences fixed while clear spoken cadence, fragments, and changes in pace remain intact?

## Words to cut

1. Are banned words, filler phrases, often-empty adverbs, and inflated claims removed unless quoted as examples?

## Patterns to cut

1. Are binary contrasts, negative listings, rhetorical setups, and throat-clearing openers removed?
2. Are faux-insight setups, colon reveals, superficial analysis, fake-strong verbs, synonym cycling, dramatic fragments, and robotic rhythm fixed?
3. Are importance puffery and weasel attribution replaced with plain facts and named sources, or flagged for the user when no source exists?
4. Are fake-profound kicker lines deleted instead of rewritten into better metaphors?
5. Are summary-recap endings cut so the piece ends on a concrete point, takeaway, or next action?
6. Is formatting slop removed: Emoji headings, decorative bold, bullets that should be prose, headers over tiny sections?
7. Are colons sentence case unless grammar, a proper noun, a title, or code requires otherwise?
8. Are em dashes used sparingly: Usually none in short copy, and only 1-2 in longer drafts when they clearly help?

## Final read

1. Was the edit checked directly against this file without requiring separate editor and evaluator agents?
2. Does the draft avoid robotic symmetry, repeated sentence shapes, and stacked punchy fragments?
3. Would the writer recognize the edited draft as their own voice?
4. Would the edited draft sound natural if read to a sharp colleague?
5. Does the final output include the full edited draft and a short **What changed** section?
6. For detect requests, does the response name each pattern with a quoted line and a short fix, without rewriting, scoring, or claiming AI authorship?
"""Apply the user's simulator geometry and response profile with rollback."""
from datetime import datetime
import hashlib
import json
import re
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
import yaml

WS = Path('/home/robot/vacuum_ws')
PACKAGE = WS / 'src/vacuum_sim'
XACRO = 'http://www.ros.org/wiki/xacro'
ET.register_namespace('xacro', XACRO)


def apply_profile():
    source = WS / 'tools/robot-profile.json'
    profile = json.loads(source.read_text())
    fingerprint = hashlib.sha256(source.read_bytes()+Path(__file__).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
    marker = WS / '.lab/hardware-profile-v2'
    if marker.exists() and marker.read_text().splitlines()[0] == fingerprint:
        return
    hardware, drive = profile['hardware'], profile['drive']
    radius = hardware['wheel_diameter_m'] / 2
    model = PACKAGE / 'urdf/vacuum.urdf.xacro'
    root = ET.fromstring(model.read_text())
    properties = {item.get('name'): item for item in root.findall(f'{{{XACRO}}}property')}
    for name, value in {'wheel_radius': radius, 'wheel_separation': hardware['wheel_separation_m'],
                        'body_z': .08, 'body_mass': 3.0}.items():
        properties[name].set('value', str(value))
    root.find("joint[@name='base_joint']/origin").set('xyz', '-0.03 0 0.116')
    wheel_macro = root.find(f'{{{XACRO}}}macro[@name="wheel"]')
    wheel_macro.find('joint/origin').set('xyz', '0.03 ${sign*wheel_separation/2} ${wheel_radius-0.116}')
    wheel_macro.find('joint/limit').set('velocity', '70.0')
    root.find("joint[@name='caster_joint']/origin").set('xyz', '-0.105 0 -0.096')
    body = root.find("link[@name='base_link']")
    for visual in list(body.findall('visual')):
        body.remove(visual)
    for name, rgba in {'acrylic': '.17 .70 .77 .55', 'rubber': '.055 .065 .075 1',
                       'sensor': '.08 .10 .14 1', 'aluminium': '.62 .68 .75 1',
                       'pcb': '.06 .42 .25 1', 'pcb_blue': '.06 .25 .52 1',
                       'copper': '.95 .58 .18 1', 'terminal': '.15 .61 .29 1'}.items():
        material = root.find(f"material[@name='{name}']")
        if material is None:
            material = ET.SubElement(root, 'material', name=name)
            ET.SubElement(material, 'color')
        material.find('color').set('rgba', rgba)

    def visual(link, name, position, shape, dimensions, material, rpy=None):
        item = ET.SubElement(link, 'visual', name=name)
        origin = ET.SubElement(item, 'origin', xyz=' '.join(map(str, position)))
        if rpy:
            origin.set('rpy', rpy)
        geometry = ET.SubElement(item, 'geometry')
        if shape == 'box':
            ET.SubElement(geometry, 'box', size=' '.join(map(str, dimensions)))
        else:
            ET.SubElement(geometry, 'cylinder', radius=str(dimensions[0]), length=str(dimensions[1]))
        ET.SubElement(item, 'material', name=material)

    for name, height in [('lower_acrylic_chassis', -.038), ('upper_acrylic_chassis', .038)]:
        visual(body, name, (0, 0, height), 'cylinder', (.15, .004), 'acrylic')
    for x in (-.08, .08):
        for y in (-.075, .075):
            visual(body, f'standoff_{x}_{y}', (x, y, 0), 'cylinder', (.004, .072), 'aluminium')

    # Fixed components remain explicit ROS links; main chassis envelope provides
    # collision volume for the electronics. Mass and module details are estimates.
    names = ('left_nema17', 'right_nema17', 'left_tb6600', 'right_tb6600', 'arduino_mega', 'orange_pi5')
    for child in list(root):
        if child.tag in ('joint', 'link') and child.get('name', '').replace('_mount', '') in names:
            root.remove(child)

    def component(name, position, dimensions, material, mass):
        joint = ET.SubElement(root, 'joint', name=name+'_mount', type='fixed')
        ET.SubElement(joint, 'parent', link='base_link'); ET.SubElement(joint, 'child', link=name)
        ET.SubElement(joint, 'origin', xyz=' '.join(map(str, position)))
        link = ET.SubElement(root, 'link', name=name)
        inertial = ET.SubElement(link, 'inertial'); ET.SubElement(inertial, 'mass', value=str(mass))
        x,y,z = dimensions
        ET.SubElement(inertial, 'inertia', ixx=str(mass*(y*y+z*z)/12),
                      iyy=str(mass*(x*x+z*z)/12), izz=str(mass*(x*x+y*y)/12), ixy='0', ixz='0', iyz='0')
        visual(link, name+'_body', (0,0,0), 'box', dimensions, material)
        return link

    for side, sign in [('left', 1), ('right', -1)]:
        motor = component(side+'_nema17', (.03, sign*.071, -.081), (.0423,.040,.0423), 'sensor', .25)
        for y in (-.016,.016):
            visual(motor, 'endplate_'+str(y), (0,y,0), 'box', (.0423,.008,.0423), 'aluminium')
        visual(motor, 'shaft_and_hub', (0,sign*.031,0), 'cylinder', (.004,.023), 'aluminium', '${pi/2} 0 0')
        visual(motor, 'under_chassis_mount', (0,0,.030), 'box', (.043,.042,.018), 'aluminium')
        driver = component(side+'_tb6600', (.078,sign*.044,-.021), (.077,.038,.026), 'sensor', .10)
        for x in (-.025,-.015,-.005,.005,.015,.025):
            visual(driver,'cooling_fin_'+str(x),(x,0,.016),'box',(.003,.038,.009),'aluminium')
        visual(driver, 'screw_terminals', (0,-sign*.022,0), 'box', (.065,.010,.018), 'terminal')
    mega = component('arduino_mega', (-.044,.056,-.027), (.10152,.0533,.003), 'pcb_blue', .037)
    visual(mega,'mega_processor',(-.009,0,.004),'box',(.014,.014,.005),'sensor')
    for y in (-.023,.023): visual(mega,'mega_pin_headers_'+str(y),(0,y,.005),'box',(.079,.004,.007),'sensor')
    visual(mega,'mega_usb',(-.046,0,.007),'box',(.015,.013,.012),'aluminium')
    orange = component('orange_pi5',(-.044,-.054,-.027),(.100,.062,.003),'pcb',.046)
    visual(orange,'rk3588s_heatsink',(0,0,.009),'box',(.025,.025,.016),'aluminium')
    for x in (-.01,-.005,0,.005,.01): visual(orange,'heatsink_fin_'+str(x),(x,0,.019),'box',(.002,.025,.006),'sensor')
    visual(orange,'ethernet_port',(-.04,0,.007),'box',(.019,.016,.014),'aluminium')
    visual(orange,'gpio_header',(.009,.026,.006),'box',(.05,.005,.009),'sensor')
    lidar = root.find("link[@name='lidar_link']")
    for item in list(lidar.findall('visual')): lidar.remove(item)
    visual(lidar,'rplidar_mount_standoff',(0,0,-.030),'cylinder',(.010,.032),'aluminium')
    visual(lidar,'rplidar_c1_base',(0,0,-.009),'box',(.054,.054,.012),'sensor')
    visual(lidar,'rplidar_c1_scanner',(0,0,.005),'cylinder',(.027,.025),'sensor')
    visual(lidar,'rplidar_c1_accent',(0,0,.015),'cylinder',(.025,.004),'copper')
    sensor = root.find("gazebo[@reference='lidar_link']/sensor")
    sensor.find('update_rate').text=str(profile['lidar']['scan_hz'])
    sensor.find('lidar/scan/horizontal/samples').text=str(profile['lidar']['samples'])
    sensor.find('lidar/range/min').text=str(profile['lidar']['min_range_m'])
    sensor.find('lidar/range/max').text=str(profile['lidar']['max_range_m'])
    sensor.find('lidar/noise/stddev').text='0.015'
    ET.indent(root, space='  ')
    updates = {model: ET.tostring(root, encoding='unicode')+'\n',
               PACKAGE/'config/robot-profile.json': json.dumps(profile,indent=2)+'\n'}
    controller = PACKAGE/'config/controllers.yaml'
    data=yaml.safe_load(controller.read_text()); p=data['diff_drive_controller']['ros__parameters']
    p.update(wheel_radius=radius, wheel_separation=hardware['wheel_separation_m'],
             publish_rate=60.0, cmd_vel_timeout=.25, velocity_rolling_window_size=drive['odometry_window_samples'])
    data['controller_manager']['ros__parameters']['update_rate']=60
    p.update({'linear.x.max_velocity':drive['forward_m_s'], 'linear.x.min_velocity':-drive['reverse_m_s'],
              'linear.x.max_acceleration':drive['acceleration_m_s2'], 'linear.x.min_acceleration':-drive['acceleration_m_s2'],
              'linear.x.has_jerk_limits':False, 'angular.z.max_velocity':drive['turn_rad_s'],
              'angular.z.min_velocity':-drive['turn_rad_s'], 'angular.z.max_acceleration':drive['angular_acceleration_rad_s2'],
              'angular.z.min_acceleration':-drive['angular_acceleration_rad_s2'], 'angular.z.has_jerk_limits':False})
    updates[controller]=yaml.safe_dump(data,sort_keys=False)
    adapter=PACKAGE/'scripts/twist_adapter.py'
    adapter_text=adapter.read_text().replace('enforces its 0.5 s timeout','enforces its 0.25 s timeout')
    adapter_text=re.sub(r'outgoing.twist.linear.x = .+',
                        f"outgoing.twist.linear.x = max(-{drive['reverse_m_s']}, min({drive['forward_m_s']}, message.linear.x))",adapter_text)
    adapter_text=re.sub(r'outgoing.twist.angular.z = .+',
                        f"outgoing.twist.angular.z = max(-{drive['turn_rad_s']}, min({drive['turn_rad_s']}, message.angular.z))",adapter_te

def prepare():
    model = PACKAGE / 'urdf/vacuum.urdf.xacro'
    marker = WS / '.lab/circular-model-v1'
    prepare_driving_views()
    from apply_robot_profile import apply_profile
    apply_profile()
    if marker.exists():
        return
    root = ET.fromstring(model.read_text())
    props = {p.get('name'): p for p in root.findall(f'{{{XACRO}}}property')}
    for key in ('body_x', 'body_y', 'body_z', 'body_mass', 'wheel_separation'):
        if key not in props:
            raise RuntimeError(f'Unexpected robot model: missing {key}; no geometry changes applied.')
    props['wheel_separation'].set('value', '0.22')
    body = root.find("link[@name='base_link']")
    if body is None:
        raise RuntimeError('Expected chassis link was not found.')
    root.find("joint[@name='base_joint']/origin").set('xyz', '-0.03 0 0.08')
    inertia = body.find('inertial/inertia')
    inertia.set('ixx', '${body_mass*(3*0.15**2+body_z**2)/12}')
    inertia.set('iyy', '${body_mass*(3*0.15**2+body_z**2)/12}')
    inertia.set('izz', '${body_mass*0.15**2/2}')
    geom = body.find('collision/geometry')
    geom.clear()
    ET.SubElement(geom, 'cylinder', radius='0.15', length='${body_z}')
    plates = 0
    for visual in body.findall('visual'):
        geom = visual.find('geometry')
        box = geom.find('box')
        if box is not None and 'body_x' in box.get('size', ''):
            geom.clear()
            ET.SubElement(geom, 'cylinder', radius='0.15', length='0.004')
            plates += 1
        elif geom.find('cylinder') is not None:
            plate = geom.find('cylinder')
            if plate.get('radius') == '0.15' and plate.get('length') == '0.004':
                plates += 1
    if plates != 2:
        raise RuntimeError('Expected two acrylic plates; no geometry changes applied.')
    wheel = root.find(f'{{{XACRO}}}macro[@name="wheel"]/joint/origin')
    wheel.set('xyz', '0.03 ${sign*wheel_separation/2} ${wheel_radius-0.08}')
    root.find("joint[@name='caster_joint']/origin").set('xyz', '-0.105 0 -0.06')
    root.find("joint[@name='camera_joint']/origin").set('xyz', '0.1325 0 0.025')
    updates = {model: ET.tostring(root, encoding='unicode') + '\n'}
    controllers = PACKAGE / 'config/controllers.yaml'
    data = yaml.safe_load(controllers.read_text())
    data['diff_drive_controller']['ros__parameters']['wheel_separation'] = .22
    updates[controllers] = yaml.safe_dump(data, sort_keys=False)
    for name in ('nav2.yaml', 'vacuum_nav2.yaml'):
        path = PACKAGE / 'config' / name
        data = yaml.safe_load(path.read_text())
        for costmap in ('local_costmap', 'global_costmap'):
            params = data[costmap][costmap]['ros__parameters']
            params.pop('robot_radius', None)
            params['footprint'] = str(circle(.15))
            params['footprint_padding'] = .02
        params = data['collision_monitor']['ros__parameters']
        if name == 'vacuum_nav2.yaml':
            params['cmd_vel_in_topic'] = '/vacuum/selected_cmd_vel'
        for zone, radius in (('StopZone', .23), ('SlowZone', .35)):
            if zone in params:
                params[zone]['points'] = str(circle(radius))
        updates[path] = yaml.safe_dump(data, sort_keys=False)
    view = PACKAGE / 'config/view.rviz'
    data = yaml.safe_load(view.read_text())
    data['Visualization Manager']['Global Options']['Fixed Frame'] = 'map'
    updates[view] = yaml.safe_dump(data, sort_keys=False)
    backup = WS / 'model-backups' / datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d-%H%M%S-%f')
    backup.mkdir(parents=True)
    originals = {path: path.read_bytes() for path in updates}
    for path, content in originals.items():
        saved = backup / path.relative_to(PACKAGE)
        saved.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        saved.write_bytes(content)
    try:
        for path, text in updates.items():
            path.write_text(text)
        built = subprocess.run(['/bin/bash', '-lc',
                                'source env.sh; colcon build --symlink-install --packages-select vacuum_sim'],
                               cwd=WS, text=True, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, timeout=180)
        if built.returncode:
            raise RuntimeError('Model build failed: ' + built.stdout[-5000:])
        marker.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        marker.write_text('30 cm circular body; axle offset 3 cm; wheel separation 22 cm.\n'
                          f'Previous source files: {backup}\n'
                          'Previous navigation validation used the old body; rerun for this geometry.\n')
    except BaseException:
        for path, content in originals.items():
            path.write_bytes(content)
        raise
    print(f'30 cm circular chassis prepared. Previous source saved in {backup}', flush=True)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    prepare()

"""Convert the checked ROS model into an editable assembly without losing detail."""
import json
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

repo = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / 'outputs/RobotLab'
templates = repo / 'designer/templates'
templates.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
source = repo / 'designs/reference.urdf'
shutil.copy2(source, templates / 'reference.urdf')
root = ET.parse(source).getroot()
materials = {e.get('name'): e.find('color').get('rgba') for e in root.findall('material') if e.find('color') is not None}
base = [-.03, 0, .116]

def numbers(text):
    return [float(x) for x in text.split()]

def visual(element):
    geom = element.find('geometry')[0]
    if geom.tag == 'box':
        size = numbers(geom.get('size'))
    elif geom.tag == 'cylinder':
        size = [float(geom.get('radius')) * 2] * 2 + [float(geom.get('length'))]
    elif geom.tag == 'sphere':
        size = [float(geom.get('radius')) * 2] * 3
    else:
        raise ValueError(geom.tag)
    origin = element.find('origin')
    material = element.find('material')
    color = material.find('color') if material is not None else None
    rgba = color.get('rgba') if color is not None else materials.get(material.get('name'), '.4 .5 .6 1') if material is not None else '.4 .5 .6 1'
    return {'shape': geom.tag, 'size_m': size,
            'xyz_m': numbers(origin.get('xyz', '0 0 0')) if origin is not None else [0, 0, 0],
            'rpy_rad': numbers(origin.get('rpy', '0 0 0')) if origin is not None else [0, 0, 0], 'rgba': numbers(rgba)}

labels = {'left_nema17': 'Left NEMA 17', 'right_nema17': 'Right NEMA 17', 'left_tb6600': 'Left TB6600',
          'right_tb6600': 'Right TB6600', 'arduino_mega': 'Arduino Mega 2560', 'orange_pi5': 'Orange Pi 5',
          'lidar_link': 'RPLIDAR C1', 'camera_link': 'Front camera', 'caster': 'Caster',
          'left_wheel': 'Left drive wheel', 'right_wheel': 'Right drive wheel'}
parts = []
for link in root.findall('link'):
    name = link.get('name')
    visuals = link.findall('visual')
    if not visuals:
        continue
    if name == 'base_link':
        for index, item in enumerate(visuals):
            v = visual(item)
            id_ = item.get('name') or f'chassis_{index}'
            id_ = id_.replace('-', 'neg').replace('.', '_')
            parts.append({'id': id_, 'label': item.get('name', id_).replace('_', ' ').title(), 'kind': 'chassis' if 'chassis' in id_ else 'standoff',
                          'role': 'fixed', 'shape': v['shape'], 'size_m': v['size_m'],
                          'xyz_m': [base[i] + v['xyz_m'][i] for i in range(3)], 'rpy_rad': v['rpy_rad'],
                          'rgba': v['rgba'], 'mass_kg': .15 if 'chassis' in id_ else .01, 'collision': 'chassis' in id_,
                          'target': {'link': name, 'visual': item.get('name')}, 'visuals': []})
        continue
    joint = next(e for e in root.findall('joint') if e.find('child').get('link') == name)
    origin = joint.find('origin')
    xyz = numbers(origin.get('xyz', '0 0 0'))
    p = {'id': name, 'label': labels.get(name, name.replace('_', ' ').title()), 'kind': name,
         'role': {'left_wheel': 'left_wheel', 'right_wheel': 'right_wheel', 'lidar_link': 'lidar', 'camera_link': 'camera'}.get(name, 'fixed'),
         'shape': 'assembly', 'xyz_m': [base[i] + xyz[i] for i in range(3)],
         'rpy_rad': numbers(origin.get('rpy', '0 0 0')), 'rgba': visual(visuals[0])['rgba'],
         'size_m': visual(visuals[0])['size_m'], 'mass_kg': float(link.find('inertial/mass').get('value')),
         'collision': link.find('collision') is not None, 'target': {'link': name}, 'visuals': [visual(v) for v in visuals]}
    parts.append(p)
design = {'schema_version': 1, 'name': 'Your vacuum robot', 'parts': parts, 'notes': 'Dimensions and masses are editable estimates. Coordinates: X forward, Y left, Z up; metres and radians in JSON.'}
(repo / 'designs/default.json').write_text(json.dumps(design, indent=2) + '\n')
print(f'Created editable assembly with {len(parts)} parts.')

      install_requires=['setuptools', 'pyserial'], zip_safe=True,
      maintainer='Robot Lab owner', maintainer_email='[REDACTED_EMAIL]',
      description='Orange Pi / Mega differential drive', license='MIT',
      entry_points={'console_scripts': ['motor_bridge = vacuum_hardware.motor_bridge:main']})
"""Hardware-only ROS package; simulator tools never import this package."""

"""ROS velocity -> Mega pulses. Arms explicitly and publishes issued-step odometry.

No encoder feedback exists in the specified hardware. /odom and joint_states are
therefore estimates; slipping wheels/missed steps cannot be observed here.
"""
import json
import math
import time
import rclpy
from rclpy.node import Node
from rclpy.qos import qos_profile_sensor_data
from geometry_msgs.msg import Twist, TransformStamped
from nav_msgs.msg import Odometry
from sensor_msgs.msg import JointState, LaserScan
from std_msgs.msg import String
from std_srvs.srv import SetBool
from lifecycle_msgs.srv import GetState
from tf2_ros import TransformBroadcaster
from .protocol import wheel_rates, count_delta
from .serial_link import SerialLink


class MotorBridge(Node):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__('motor_bridge')
        defaults = {'serial_port': '/dev/robot_mega', 'serial_baud': 115200, 'motion_enabled': False,
                    'wheel_radius_m': .035, 'wheel_separation_m': .22, 'steps_per_revolution': 1600,
                    'forward_m_s': .15, 'reverse_m_s': .08, 'turn_rad_s': .8, 'command_timeout_s': .25,
                    'scan_timeout_s': .5, 'acceleration_m_s2': .4, 'angular_acceleration_rad_s2': 1.5}
        self.settings = {k: self.declare_parameter(k, v).value for k, v in defaults.items()}
        for key in defaults:
            if key not in ('serial_port', 'motion_enabled') and (not math.isfinite(self.settings[key]) or self.settings[key] <= 0):
                raise ValueError(f'{key} must be positive and finite.')
        self.link = SerialLink(self.settings['serial_port'], self.settings['serial_baud'])
        self.armed = False; self.handshake = False; self.reason = 'Disarmed'
        self.velocity = [0., 0.]; self.command = [0., 0.]; self.command_at = 0.; self.scan_at = 0.
        self.guard_active = False; self.guard_at = 0.; self.guard_future = None; self.guard_sent = 0.
        self.pose = [0., 0., 0.]; self.previous_steps = None; self.odom_at = 0.; self.last_report = 0.
        self.received_sequence = None
        self.create_subscription(Twist, '/cmd_vel', self.on_command, 1)
        self.create_subscription(LaserScan, '/scan', self.on_scan, qos_profile_sensor_data)
        self.create_service(SetBool, '/drive/arm', self.on_arm)
        self.guard_client = self.create_client(GetState, '/collision_monitor/get_state')
        self.odom = self.create_publisher(Odometry, '/odom', 10)
        self.joints = self.create_publisher(JointState, '/joint_states', 10)
        self.health = self.create_publisher(String, '/drive/status', 10)
        self.tf = TransformBroadcaster(self)
        self.last_tick = time.monotonic(); self.timer = self.create_timer(.02, self.tick)

    def disarm(self, reason):
        self.armed = False; self.handshake = False; self.velocity = [0., 0.]; self.reason = reason
        self.link.update(False, 0, 0)

    def on_command(self, msg):
        if not math.isfinite(msg.linear.x) or not math.isfinite(msg.angular.z):
            self.disarm('Nonfinite velocity'); return
        p = self.settings
        self.command = [max(-p['reverse_m_s'], min(p['forward_m_s'], msg.linear.x)),
                        max(-p['turn_rad_s'], min(p['turn_rad_s'], msg.angular.z))]
        self.command_at = time.monotonic()

    def on_scan(self, msg):
        # Empty/invalid scans cannot keep the motor guard alive.
        if msg.ranges and any(math.isfinite(x) and msg.range_min <= x <= msg.range_max for x in msg.ranges):
            self.scan_at = time.monotonic()

    def ready(self, now, status, received):
        return status is not None and now-received < .25 and status.fault == 0 and now-self.scan_at < self.settings['scan_timeout_s'] and self.guard_active and now-self.guard_at < 1.5

    def on_arm(self, request, response):
        if not request.data:
            self.disarm('Disarmed by user'); response.success = True; response.message = self.reason; return response
        now = time.monotonic(); connected, status, received, error = self.link.snapshot()
        if not self.settings['motion_enabled']: response.message = 'Set motion_enabled after wiring and wheel calibration.'
        elif not connected or not self.ready(now, status, received): response.message = 'Mega, lidar or collision guard is not ready. ' + error
        elif now-self.command_at < self.settings['command_timeout_s'] and any(abs(x) > .001 for x in self.command): response.message = 'Centre the drive command before arming.'
        else:
            self.armed = True; self.handshake = False; self.reason = 'Armed at zero'; response.success = True; response.message = self.reason
        return response

    def tick(self):
        now = time.monotonic(); dt = min(.05, now-self.last_tick); self.last_tick = now
        if self.guard_future:
            if self.guard_future.done():
                try: self.guard_active = self.guard_future.result().current_state.id == 3; self.guard_at = now
                except Exception: self.guard_active = False
                self.guard_future = None
            elif now-self.guard_sent > .75:
                self.guard_client.remove_pending_request(self.guard_future); self.guard_future = None; self.guard_active = False
        elif now-self.guard_sent > .5 and self.guard_client.service_is_ready():
            self.guard_sent = now; self.guard_future = self.guard_client.call_async(GetState.Request())
        connected, status, received, error = self.link.snapshot()
        if self.armed:
            if not connected or not self.ready(now, status, received): self.disarm('Hardware/guard health lost: ' + error)
            elif now-self.command_at > self.settings['command_timeout_s'] and self.handshake: self.disarm('Drive input expired')
        if self.armed:
            if not self.handshake:
                self.link.update(True, 0, 0)
                if status.armed: self.handshake = True; self.command_at = now
            else:
                for i, acceleration in enumerate((self.settings['acceleration_m_s2'], self.settings['angular_acceleration_rad_s2'])):
                    self.velocity[i] += max(-acceleration*dt, min(acceleration*dt, self.command[i]-self.velocity[i]))
                left, right = wheel_rates(*self.velocity, self.settings['wheel_radius_m'], self.settings['wheel_separation_m'], self.settings['steps_per_revolution'])
                self.link.update(True, left, right)
        else: self.link.update(False, 0, 0)
        if status and received != self.last_report:
            self.publish_odometry(status, received); self.last_report = received
        if int(now*5) != int((now-dt)*5):
            self.health.publish(String(data=json.dumps({'armed':self.armed,'ready':self.ready(now,status,received),
                'reason':self.reason,'serial_error':error,'firmware_fault':status.fault if status else None,'odometry':'issued steps; no encoders'})))

    def publish_odometry(self, status, received):
        counts = [status.left_steps, status.right_steps]
        if self.previous_steps is None or received-self.odom_at > .5:
            self.previous_steps = counts; self.odom_at = received; return
        delta = [count_delta(counts[i], self.previous_steps[i]) for i in range(2)]
        self.previous_steps = counts
        dt = max(.001, received-self.odom_at); self.odom_at = received
        metres = 2*math.pi*self.settings['wheel_radius_m']/self.settings['steps_per_revolution']
        dl, dr = [x*metres for x in delta]; distance=(dl+dr)/2; angle=(dr-dl)/self.settings['wheel_separation_m']
        # Reject counter resets/jumps rather than teleporting odometry on USB reset.
        if abs(dl)>dt*.5+.03 or abs(dr)>dt*.5+.03: self.disarm('Unexpected step counter reset'); return
        self.pose[0] += distance*math.cos(self.pose[2]+angle/2); self.pose[1] += distance*math.sin(self.pose[2]+angle/2); self.pose[2] += angle
        stamp = self.get_clock().now().to_msg()
        odom=Odometry(); odom.header.stamp=stamp; odom.header.frame_id='odom'; odom.child_frame_id='base_footprint'
        odom.pose.pose.position.x,odom.pose.pose.position.y=self.pose[:2]
        odom.pose.pose.orientation.z=math.sin(self.pose[2]/2); odom.pose.pose.orientation.w=math.cos(self.pose[2]/2)
        odom.twist.twist.linear.x=distance/dt; odom.twist.twist.angular.z=angle/dt
        for i in (0,7): odom.pose.covariance[i]=.05; odom.twist.covariance[i]=.05
        odom.pose.covariance[35]=.1; odom.twist.covariance[35]=.1
        self.odom.publish(odom)
        tf=TransformStamped(); tf.header=odom.header; tf.child_frame_id=odom.child_frame_id
        tf.transform.translation.x,tf.transform.translation.y=self.pose[:2]; tf.transform.rotation=odom.pose.pose.orientation; self.tf.sendTransform(tf)
        joints=JointState(); joints.header.stamp=stamp; joints.name=['left_wheel_joint','right_wheel_joint']
        joints.position=[x*2*math.pi/self.settings['steps_per_revolution'] for x in counts]; self.joints.publish(joints)

    def destroy_node(self):
        self.disarm('Bridge shutdown'); self.link.close(); super().destroy_node()


def main():
    rclpy.init(); node = MotorBridge()
    try: rclpy.spin(node)
    except KeyboardInterrupt: pass
    finally: node.destroy_node(); rclpy.try_shutdown()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Copy a chosen design into the hardware package; preserve physical speed caps."""
import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path
import sys

repo = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
sys.path.insert(0, str(repo/'designer'))
from model import compile_model, drive_geometry, footprint, hardware_description

def main():
    import yaml
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument('design', type=Path)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    design = json.loads(args.design.read_text())
    geometry = drive_geometry(design)
    urdf, meshes = compile_model(design)
    package = repo/'ros2/src/vacuum_hardware'
    (package/'urdf/robot.urdf').write_text(hardware_description(urdf))
    for name, data in meshes.items():
        destination = package/'meshes/design'/name
        destination.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True); destination.write_bytes(data)
    config_path = package/'config/hardware.yaml'
    data = yaml.safe_load(config_path.read_text()); params = data['motor_bridge']['ros__parameters']
    params.update(wheel_radius_m=geometry['wheel_radius_m'], wheel_separation_m=geometry['wheel_separation_m'], motion_enabled=False)
    fp = footprint(design)
    xs, ys = [p[0] for p in fp], [p[1] for p in fp]
    data['collision_monitor']['ros__parameters']['StopZone']['points'] = str([
        [min(xs)-.15,min(ys)-.05],[max(xs)+.15,min(ys)-.05],[max(xs)+.15,max(ys)+.05],[min(xs)-.15,max(ys)+.05]])
    config_path.write_text(yaml.safe_dump(data,sort_keys=False))
    print('Hardware model and geometry updated. Motion stays disabled until calibration.')

if __name__ == '__main__': main()

"""Serial-worker heartbeat and shutdown checks with an in-memory Mega."""
from pathlib import Path
import sys
import threading
import time
import unittest

repo=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0,str(repo/'ros2/src/vacuum_hardware'))
from vacuum_hardware.protocol import frame
from vacuum_hardware.serial_link import SerialLink


class FakeMega:
    def __init__(self): self.lock=threading.Lock(); self.buffer=b''; self.commands=[]; self.closed=False
    def write(self,packet):
        fields=packet.decode().strip().split(',')
        with self.lock:
            self.commands.append(fields)
            self.buffer+=frame(f'S1,{fields[1]},{fields[2]},0,0,0')
        return len(packet)
    @property
    def in_waiting(self):
        with self.lock: return len(self.buffer)
    def read(self,size):
        with self.lock: data=self.buffer[:size];self.buffer=self.buffer[size:];return data
    def close(self): self.closed=True


class LinkTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_heartbeat_and_shutdown(self):
        mega=FakeMega(); link=SerialLink('fake',factory=lambda:mega)
        try:
            for _ in range(30):

        self.node=MotorBridge();now=time.monotonic();self.node.scan_at=self.node.guard_at=now;self.node.guard_active=True

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Install this repository's simulator source into a selected ROS workspace.

The source tree is copied, not linked across Windows/WSL. Existing source/tools
are backed up first. Applied designs remain selected across launcher updates.
"""
import argparse
from datetime import datetime
import json
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys

repo = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0,str(repo/'designer'))
from model import compile_model


def main():
    parser=argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument('--workspace',type=Path,required=True)
    args=parser.parse_args(); workspace=args.workspace.expanduser().resolve()
    if not (workspace/'env.sh').exists():
        workspace.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
        (workspace/'env.sh').write_text('''#!/usr/bin/env bash
export ROS_AUTOMATIC_DISCOVERY_RANGE=LOCALHOST
export ROS_DOMAIN_ID=42
export GZ_PARTITION=vacuum_sim_42
export GZ_IP=127.0.0.1
source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash
robot_workspace="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
if [[ -f "$robot_workspace/install/setup.bash" ]]; then source "$robot_workspace/install/setup.bash"; fi
unset robot_workspace
''')
    state=workspace/'.lab';state.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    if (state/'processes.json').exists():
        result=subprocess.run(['python3','tools/lab_controller.py','stop'],cwd=workspace)
        if result.returncode: raise SystemExit('Stop the current simulator before updating source.')
    backup=workspace/'model-backups'/('source-update-'+datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d-%H%M%S-%f'))
    for name in ('src/vacuum_sim','tools'):
        path=workspace/name
        if path.exists(): shutil.copytree(path,backup/name,ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns('__pycache__'))
    selected=json.loads((state/'custom-design.json').read_text()) if (state/'custom-design.json').exists() else None
    shutil.copytree(repo/'ros2/src/vacuum_sim',workspace/'src/vacuum_sim',dirs_exist_ok=True)
    shutil.copytree(repo/'simulation/tools',workspace/'tools',dirs_exist_ok=True,ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns('__pycache__'))
    if not selected:
        shutil.copy2(repo/'config/simulation.json',workspace/'tools/robot-profile.json')
        model,meshes=compile_model(json.loads((repo/'designs/default.json').read_text()))
        (workspace/'src/vacuum_sim/urdf/designed.urdf').write_text(model)
    else:
        model,meshes=compile_model(selected['design'])
        (workspace/'src/vacuum_sim/urdf/designed.urdf').write_text(model)
    for name,data in meshes.items():
        path=workspace/'src/vacuum_sim/meshes/design'/name;path.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True);path.write_bytes(data)
    result=subprocess.run(['/bin/bash','-lc','source env.sh; colcon build --symlink-install --packages-select vacuum_sim'],cwd=workspace)
    if result.returncode: raise SystemExit(f'Build failed. Source backup: {backup}')
    print(f'Simulation installed in {workspace}. Previous source: {backup}')


if __name__=='__main__':main()

# Robot Lab

Open **Vacuum Lab.exe** beside this folder. Choose **Design robot** to edit the assembly, **Drive now** to test it, or **All project files** to find the source and saved data. The Windows app uses the existing `VacuumRobot-24.04` WSL installation.

The supplied robot has two NEMA 17 motors below its acrylic chassis, two 70 mm wheels, two TB6600 drivers, an Arduino Mega 2560, an Orange Pi 5 and an RPLIDAR C1. Manual simulation runs in a 16 × 12 m room at up to 1.5 m/s forward. Arm once and centre the yoke to stop; holding a drive button is optional.

## Where things live

| Folder | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `desktop/` | Windows launcher, yoke control and file browser |
| `designer/` | Offline 3D editor, save API and model exporter |
| `designs/` | Supplied editable design |
| `config/` | Simulator profile and pinned dependency versions |
| `ros2/src/vacuum_sim/` | Gazebo model, world, controllers, mapping and navigation |
| `ros2/src/vacuum_hardware/` | Orange Pi serial bridge, physical configuration and launch |
| `ros2/src/sllidar_ros2/` | Official SLAMTEC driver, pinned to the recorded commit |
| `firmware/mega_drive/` | Mega sketch, motor settings and serial protocol |
| `simulation/tools/` | Simulator startup, command guard and motion checks |
| `tools/deploy/` | Orange Pi setup, build, run and design export |
| `docs/` | Instructions and interface reference |
| `tests/` | Model, protocol, firmware and ROS checks |
| `assets/` | Preview images, app icon and editor screenshot |
| `reports/` | Current checks and historical measurements |
| `archive/` | Earlier files, preserved for reference |

Saved designs and their history live in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\VacuumLab\designs`. They survive executable updates. The live simulator workspace remains `/home/robot/vacuum_ws`; its logs, maps and model backups are runtime data, rather than source files.

## Start with the task you need

- [Move parts, add shapes or import STL](docs/designer.md)
- [Transfer the project to the Orange Pi](docs/orange-pi.md)
- [Wire and configure the Mega and TB6600s](docs/hardware.md)
- [Understand the control paths and serial messages](docs/architecture.md)
- [Build, test and maintain the code](docs/development.md)
- [See the checks and remaining limits](reports/README.md)

Component dimensions and masses are editable estimates. The physical profile starts at 0.15 m/s and with motion disabled. Simulation at 1.5 m/s does not establish that the real motor, driver and power system can achieve that speed. Issued-step odometry cannot detect wheel slip or missed steps.

# Control paths and file ownership

The desktop controller sends JSON over WSL stdin to the simulator bridge. The bridge checks input freshness, lidar freshness and guard state, then publishes the manual command source. The source gate selects manual/navigation output. Nav2 Collision Monitor filters that command before Gazebo receives it. Closing stdin, disarming or losing health produces zero.

Hardware uses a separate path: teleop `/cmd_vel_raw` → Collision Monitor `/cmd_vel` → Orange Pi `motor_bridge` → USB → Mega → two TB6600s. The motor bridge has an explicit `/drive/arm` service. It clamps physical velocities, converts differential-drive velocities to pulse rates and sends commands at 50 Hz. The serial worker has its own 200 ms caller heartbeat. The Mega also has a 350 ms command watchdog.

## Geometry and saved data

`designs/default.json` is the editable seed. A saved design records each part's dimensions, position, rotation, mass, colour and collision flag. Template attachments preserve functional wheel joints and sensor frames. New parts become fixed links. `designer/model.py` validates the format and compiles models; `designer/templates/reference.urdf` preserves the sensor/plugin detail from the checked model.

The browser uses the same X/Y/Z frame as ROS. Three.js Euler order `ZYX` implements URDF roll/pitch/yaw. Stored sizes use metres, rotations radians. Assembly geometry is a set of primitive visuals; STL geometry is stored as base64 inside the design and copied to mesh files on export. Chassis collisions and navigation footprints update conservatively from the design. Collision boxes/masses remain estimates.

Each save uses a content revision. The local API rejects stale revisions and keeps older versions. The server binds to loopback, requires a random session token for API calls, rejects foreign origins, bounds payload sizes and constrains save names. It exposes fixed operations rather than a command or arbitrary-path interface.

`config/simulation.json` owns the simulator drive defaults. `vacuum_hardware/config/hardware.yaml` owns physical geometry, limits and serial paths. `drive_config.h` owns Mega pins, pulse polarity, timing, microsteps and direction inversion. Keep steps/revolution and driver DIP settings consistent; the exporter never raises physical speed limits.

## Serial protocol, version 1

All frames are ASCII lines ending in newline. The last field is four hexadecimal digits of CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE over bytes before the final comma. Initial CRC is `0xFFFF`, polynomial `0x1021`. The check string `123456789` yields `0x29B1`.

```text
V1,sequence,enabled,left_steps_per_second,right_steps_per_second,CRC
S1,sequence,armed,fault,left_issued_steps,right_issued_steps,CRC
```

Sequence is unsigned 16-bit. Enabled/armed is 0 or 1. Command rates are signed integers capped at 16000 pulses/s per wheel. Both wheel rates scale together if a limit is reached, preserving requested curvature. Status counts are signed presentations of modular 32-bit counters. The host uses modular differences to handle rollover.

Firmware fault codes: 0 healthy; 1 boot/timeout/handshake required; 2 stop loop open; 3 malformed, corrupt or replayed enabled frame. Disabled zero frames may reset the sequence after a host restart and cannot cause motion. Re-arming requires disabled zero, then enabled zero. Replayed enabled sequences disarm.

Wheel travel is `2π × radius × issued_steps / steps_per_revolution`. The bridge integrates it into `/odom` and publishes `/joint_states` and the `odom → base_footprint` transform. This is open-loop odometry. Missing steps and slipping wheels are unobserved; scan matching can correct the mapped pose but does not measure individual wheel motion.

## Runtime processes

The simulator launcher records PID plus Linux start identity and only stops processes it owns. `run_sim.py` tracks its child sessions and retains the single-simulator lock until cleanup ends. Applied-design updates reserve the manual-input lock and refuse to rebuild while a drive panel is open. Backups stay under `model-backups/`, marked `COLCON_IGNORE` so colcon cannot mistake them for active ROS packages.

# Edit the robot

Choose **Design robot** in the launcher. The editor runs locally and loads its graphics library from this project; it needs no account or internet connection. The supplied assembly has 17 separately editable parts, including both chassis plates, standoffs, wheels, motors, drivers, boards, lidar and camera.

Click a part in the list or 3D view. Drag the coloured arrows to move it. **Move** and **Rotate** switch the handle; `W` and `E` do the same. Right-drag to orbit, middle-drag to pan and scroll to zoom. **Top**, **Front** and **Fit** change the view. Snap defaults to 5 mm, with 5-degree rotation steps; set snap to zero for free placement.

The properties panel accepts exact position in millimetres and rotation in degrees. X points forward, Y left and Z up from the floor reference. JSON stores metres and radians. Size and mass are editable. Wheel size is diameter × diameter × width; supplied wheel assemblies have a built-in 90-degree cylinder rotation, so their part rotation starts at zero.

## Add and remove parts

Choose a library part and press **Add part**. The library includes your electronics, a battery, chassis plates, a wheel housing and custom boxes, cylinders and spheres. New parts are fixed attachments. **Duplicate** copies a selected part as another fixed attachment. **Remove** removes it from the design. Undo/redo keeps the last 30 edits; keyboard shortcuts are Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y.

**Import STL** accepts a local STL up to 8 MB. Choose the file's units, then set its position and mass. Imported meshes keep their authored origin. Their dimensions define an approximate collision box; they do not calculate a measured centre of mass. A flat or invalid mesh is rejected. Use a solid mesh with thickness for a physical part.

## Save, export and simulate

**Save** writes the file name shown at the top. Enter a new name to save another design. Names accept letters, numbers, hyphens and underscores. Existing files keep timestamped copies in `history/`. Two editors cannot silently overwrite each other's changes: a conflicting save asks you to reload or choose another name. Unsaved changes produce a close/reload prompt.

**Export robot** downloads a ZIP containing `design.json`, a simulation URDF, a hardware URDF and imported meshes. **Import JSON** opens one of these design files. Exports preserve layouts that are unsuitable for differential drive, so you can keep working on them.

**Check layout** verifies wheel geometry. **Apply to simulator** saves the design, stops the owned simulator, creates a backup, updates the model/controller/obstacle footprint, rebuilds and restarts. Close the driving panel first. The update runs in the background and reports its stage. If rebuilding or startup fails, source changes roll back and the simulator stays stopped; inspect the reported error before restarting.

The simulator needs the supplied left wheel, right wheel and lidar. Both wheels must have equal diameter/width, a shared X position, parallel Y axles, and centre Z at half their diameter. Left wheel Y must exceed right wheel Y. Boards, motors, chassis and sensors can move independently. The editor checks drive geometry, not mechanical mounting strength, wiring clearance, torque or collision-free assembly.

For the Orange Pi, copy the saved JSON into this project's `designs/`, then run `python3 tools/deploy/export-hardware.py designs/your-design.json` and rebuild. This updates the physical model and wheel geometry while keeping its speed limits and disabling motion for recalibration.

# Build and maintain

The source folders are the editable project. Executable extraction and ROS build output are generated files. Change a source file, run the relevant checks, then rebuild the affected target. Keep historical reports in `reports/history/`; a report is evidence for the version/date it names.

## Simulator update

From Ubuntu/WSL with ROS/Gazebo installed:

```bash
python3 tools/install-simulation.py --workspace /home/robot/vacuum_ws
cd /home/robot/vacuum_ws
python3 tools/lab_controller.py drive
```

The installer preserves a selected assembly and backs up source/tools before updating. Stop the drive panel before installing. On this Windows PC, run it through `wsl.exe -d VacuumRobot-24.04 -u robot --exec python3` with the script's `/mnt/c/...` path. Runtime workspace paths in Python resolve through `workspace_paths.py`; `ROBOT_LAB_WORKSPACE` overrides them for another deployment.

`build_furnished_room.py` regenerates the room. Sensor/control configuration lives inside `vacuum_sim/config`. `validate_drive.py` moves the robot; run it only with the Windows drive panel closed. The simulator uses domain 42 and a local Gazebo partition. NVIDIA/WSLg renderer overrides remain in this PC's existing `env.sh`, rather than the Orange Pi scripts.

## Tests

```bash
source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash
ROS_DOMAIN_ID=43 ROS_AUTOMATIC_DISCOVERY_RANGE=LOCALHOST bash tests/run.sh
```

This runs Python model/export/save-conflict/wire/serial/ROS tests and compiles a host harness around the actual Mega sketch. The harness replaces AVR registers and serial I/O; it checks boot refusal, pulse generation, reversal, timeout, stop input, corrupt/replayed messages and reconnect. It does not establish electrical pulse shape or loaded motor behavior. Without sourced ROS, the hardware ROS tests report skipped.

The Mega target also needs an AVR compile using Arduino CLI or IDE. The official Arduino core may emit unused-parameter warnings. The official SLAMTEC source also emits upstream compiler warnings; it is pinned and kept separate from our code. Dependency versions are recorded in `config/dependencies.json`, with license files beside vendored graphics/driver source.

Own Python code is formatted with Black 25.1.0 and checked for F-series errors using Ruff 0.11.13. The editor uses Prettier 3.6.2. Vendor code is preserved as supplied. Comments describe units, ownership and failure behavior; ordinary assignments do not need narrating comments.

## Windows executable

In PowerShell:

```powershell
powershell.exe -NoProfile -File desktop\build\Build.ps1
```

The compiler embeds the separated source tree, excluding archives, ROS builds, caches and generated logs. If a sibling `RobotLab/` source folder exists, the executable opens it so edits remain visible. A standalone executable extracts its embedded tree to a versioned local cache. Saved designs and controller profiles live outside that cache. `--check --report PATH` verifies menu construction without driving; `--files`, `--drive` and `--designer` open the corresponding workflow.

To change an interface, edit both sides and add a test that would fail under the old behavior. Physical verification belongs in a separate dated report; keep the distinction between a compile, a fake-device test and a measured hardware result.

# Mega 2560 and TB6600 drive

The firmware controls one driver per NEMA 17 using step/direction signals. The Orange Pi connects to the Mega over USB and to the C1 using its USB serial adapter. No Orange Pi GPIO connection to a motor driver is needed for this implementation.

## Signal wiring

The supplied firmware assumes common-anode step/direction wiring. Check the labels and manual for your particular TB6600 module; modules sold under this name differ.

| Mega connection | Left driver | Right driver |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 5 V | PUL+ and DIR+ | PUL+ and DIR+ |
| D22 | PUL− | — |
| D23 | — | PUL− |
| D24 | DIR− | — |
| D25 | — | DIR− |
| D26 | Optional ENA− after polarity check | Optional ENA− after polarity check |

ENA is unused by default. With this setting, disarming stops pulses but does not promise removal of motor holding torque. Each driver's motor supply comes from the rated external supply, not the Mega's USB/5 V pin. Connect each motor's two coil pairs to A+/A− and B+/B− as labelled on the driver. Identify coil pairs with the motor datasheet or continuity measurement.

D27 has a pull-up and expects a normally closed stop loop to Mega GND. A closed loop is healthy; an open loop stops pulses. For a bench test, a jumper from D27 to GND closes the loop. The physical emergency-stop switch should also interrupt the motor power through a suitable circuit. The software stop input is not a substitute for cutting motor power.

## Settings to measure and check

Edit `firmware/mega_drive/drive_config.h`. Defaults are 200 full steps/revolution and 8 microsteps, so one wheel revolution needs 1600 pulses. Set both TB6600 microstep DIP switches to match. Set current according to your actual motor rating and driver instructions. The default right direction is inverted for mirrored motor mounting; verify both directions with wheels raised.

Edit `ros2/src/vacuum_hardware/config/hardware.yaml`. Match wheel radius, wheel separation and `steps_per_revolution` to the assembled robot. The supplied wheel radius is 0.035 m and separation is 0.22 m. `motion_enabled` starts false; change it after wiring and calibration checks. Physical limits start at 0.15 m/s forward, 0.08 m/s reverse and 0.8 rad/s turn.

At 1.5 m/s, a 70 mm wheel needs about 409 RPM. That simulation speed requires a loaded motor/driver/power test before use on the real chassis.

## Compile and upload

With Arduino CLI installed:

```bash
arduino-cli core install arduino:avr@1.8.8
arduino-cli compile --fqbn arduino:avr:mega firmware/mega_drive
arduino-cli board list
arduino-cli upload --fqbn arduino:avr:mega -p /dev/robot_mega firmware/mega_drive
```

Select your actual Mega port if the stable device alias has not been created yet. Alternatively open `mega_drive.ino` in the Arduino IDE, select Mega 2560, then compile/upload. Stop the ROS bridge before uploading because it owns the serial port.

Firmware boot/reset is disarmed. Valid commands require CRC, a sequence number and a fresh disabled-zero handshake followed by an enabled-zero handshake. The 40 kHz timer produces pulses of at least 25 µs with a separate low tick. It stops pulses after a 350 ms command timeout, a broken stop loop or invalid frame. The main loop ramps reversals through zero; its watchdog resets a stalled loop into disarmed boot.

Telemetry reports issued pulses. It does not confirm that the motor turned. The specified hardware has no wheel encoders; check step accuracy under load, and add encoders if you need measured wheel odometry.

The C1 configuration uses 460800 baud and its published range of 0.05–12 m. References: [SLAMTEC C1 specification](https://www.slamtec.com/en/c1/spec), [official C1 ROS launch](https://github.com/Slamtec/sllidar_ros2/blob/34300099fadfc772965962dec837bf436706188f/launch/sllidar_c1_launch.py), [DFRobot TB6600 module reference](https://wiki.dfrobot.com/dri0043). The DFRobot module is a wiring reference, not identification of your exact driver.

# Transfer to the Orange Pi 5

Copy the `RobotLab` folder or unpack the source ZIP into a directory you own, such as `~/robot-lab`. The hardware scripts resolve paths relative to that folder. They do not assume your Windows user name, WSL paths, or `/home/robot/vacuum_ws`.

Use a working Ubuntu 24.04 arm64 image for your Orange Pi 5. Jazzy supports Ubuntu Noble arm64; board boot/kernel support still depends on the image. Check with `cat /etc/os-release` and `dpkg --print-architecture`. The setup script refuses a different OS release or a 32-bit architecture.

## Install and build

From the copied folder:

```bash
bash tools/deploy/install-deps.sh
bash tools/deploy/fetch-lidar.sh
bash tools/deploy/build-hardware.sh
```

`install-deps.sh` installs the official ROS repository package and hardware dependencies using sudo. `fetch-lidar.sh` accepts the bundled SLAMTEC source, or fetches its pinned commit if missing. `build-hardware.sh` builds only the motor bridge and lidar driver; the Orange Pi does not need Gazebo.

## Stable USB device names

Connect the Mega and C1 adapter, then inspect each device:

```bash
ls -l /dev/serial/by-id/
udevadm info -a -n /dev/ttyACM0
udevadm info -a -n /dev/ttyUSB0
sudo usermod -aG dialout "$USER"
```

Use your actual port names. Edit `tools/deploy/99-robot-lab.rules.example` with each device's serial number. Copy the edited rules into `/etc/udev/rules.d/99-robot-lab.rules`, reload rules with `sudo udevadm control --reload-rules`, then reconnect the devices. Log out/in after adding the dialout group. The expected aliases are `/dev/robot_mega` and `/dev/robot_lidar`. If an adapter has no unique serial, configure its stable `/dev/serial/by-path/` path in the YAML and launch argument instead of using an ambiguous vendor/product match.

Upload the Mega sketch using [the firmware guide](hardware.md). Run `python3 tools/deploy/preflight.py` to report prerequisites. It does not open ports or move motors.

## Use your saved assembly

Copy your editor JSON into `designs/`, then:

```bash
python3 tools/deploy/export-hardware.py designs/your-design.json
bash tools/deploy/build-hardware.sh
```

The exporter updates sensor frames, geometry, wheel dimensions and the obstacle envelope. It copies imported STL files into the hardware package. Physical speed limits stay separate; motion is disabled after a model export so you can recalibrate.

## First drive

Start with wheels raised and the stop circuit working. Inspect `hardware.yaml`, confirm matching microsteps and wheel direction, then enable `motion_enabled` for the bench test. Start the bridge/lidar/obstacle monitor:

```bash
bash tools/deploy/run-hardware.sh
```

It starts disarmed. In another terminal, source `/opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash` and `ros2/install/setup.bash`, and set `ROS_DOMAIN_ID=43`. Publish zero continuously on `/cmd_vel_raw` before arming, and inspect `/drive/status`:

```bash
ros2 topic pub --rate 20 /cmd_vel_raw geometry_msgs/msg/Twist '{}'
ros2 topic echo /drive/status
ros2 service call /drive/arm std_srvs/srv/SetBool '{data: true}'
```

Use separate terminals for the continuous publisher, status and service. After the zero handshake, use a teleop publisher on `/cmd_vel_raw`. The monitor publishes filtered commands on `/cmd_vel`; a command older than 250 ms disarms the bridge. A stale scan, inactive guard, serial failure or firmware fault also disarms it. Re-arm only at neutral. Disarm with the service using `{data: false}` or open the stop loop.

Domain 43 isolates hardware from the simulator's domain 42. Discovery defaults to this computer. If you intentionally control the robot over a network, configure the same hardware domain and discovery settings on both hosts; do not carry the simulator's local-only environment into that session.

The hardware code was built/tested on the Ubuntu x86_64 development machine with fake serial devices. Orange Pi USB timing, real torque/current and loaded motion remain bench checks. [ROS Jazzy installation reference](https://docs.ros.org/en/jazzy/Installation/Ubuntu-Install-Debs.html) and [supported platforms](https://www.ros.org/reps/rep-2000.html#jazzy-jalisco-may-2024-may-2029).

# Verification scope

Current review includes the 3D editor, saved-design model compiler, Arduino firmware, Orange Pi ROS bridge, deployment scripts and reorganized executable. `quality-review.json` records the final checks and their scope.

Earlier motion/navigation/FPS results are preserved under `history/`. They measured the previous simulator build: about 61 camera FPS, forward 90% response in 0.34 seconds, directional obstacle protection, successful navigation/map save and clean simulator shutdown. The current review reruns relevant checks after model/export changes rather than treating those older results as proof for every editable assembly.

Firmware compiles for Mega 2560. Its host harness tests the actual sketch logic with fake registers. ROS serial tests use fake devices and exercise arming/timeout behavior. Both the hardware ROS package and official lidar driver build on Ubuntu x86_64. The physical robot, Orange Pi board and power electronics were not connected for testing.

Editable layouts can be mechanically impossible. Wheel alignment is checked before simulation; mounting clearances, measured mass, wiring, torque and loaded motor performance need inspection on the assembled robot. Issued-step odometry has no encoder confirmation.

def prepare_driving_views():
    launch = PACKAGE / "launch/sim.launch.py"
    text = launch.read_text()
    text = text.replace(
        "DeclareLaunchArgument('camera_rate', default_value='5')",
        "DeclareLaunchArgument('camera_rate', default_value='60')",
    )
    if "DeclareLaunchArgument('rviz_config'" not in text:
        text = text.replace(
            "DeclareLaunchArgument('rviz', default_value='true'),",
            "DeclareLaunchArgument('rviz', default_value='true'),\n"
            "        DeclareLaunchArgument('rviz_config', default_value=str(package / 'config/view.rviz')),",
        )
        text = text.replace(
            "arguments=['-d', str(package / 'config/view.rviz')]",
            "arguments=['-d', LaunchConfiguration('rviz_config')]",
        )
    compile(text, str(launch), "exec")
    model = PACKAGE / "urdf/vacuum.urdf.xacro"
    root = ET.fromstring(model.read_text())
    rate = root.find(f'{{{XACRO}}}arg[@name="camera_rate"]')
    if rate is None:
        raise RuntimeError("The camera rate argument is missing.")
    rate.set("default", "60")
    view = PACKAGE / "config/view.rviz"
    data = yaml.safe_load(view.read_text())
    data["Visualization Manager"]["Global Options"]["Frame Rate"] = 60
    drive_data = yaml.safe_load(yaml.safe_dump(data))
    drive_data["Visualization Manager"]["Global Options"]["Fixed Frame"] = "odom"
    drive_data["Visualization Manager"]["Displays"] = [
        item
        for item in drive_data["Visualization Manager"]["Displays"]
        if item.get("Class") != "rviz_default_plugins/Map"
    ]
    updates = {
        launch: text,
        model: ET.tostring(root, encoding="unicode") + "\n",
        view: yaml.safe_dump(data, sort_keys=False),
        PACKAGE / "config/drive.rviz": yaml.safe_dump(drive_data, sort_keys=False),
    }
    world = PACKAGE / "worlds/room.sdf"
    scene = ET.fromstring(world.read_text())
    # 180 Hz physics divides into 60 Hz camera/control, 30 Hz odometry, 10 Hz lidar.
    # At the 1.5 m/s limit a physics step covers about 8.3 mm.
    scene.find("world/physics/max_step_size").text = "0.005555555555555556"
    updates[world] = ET.tostring(scene, encoding="unicode") + "\n"
    changed = {
        path: value
        for path, value in updates.items()
        if not path.exists() or path.read_text() != value
    }
    if not changed:
        return
    backup = WS / "model-backups" / datetime.now().strftime("camera60-%Y%m%d-%H%M%S-%f")
    backup.mkdir(parents=True)
    originals = {path: path.read_bytes() if path.exists() else None for path in changed}
    for path, content in originals.items():
        if content is not None:
            saved = backup / path.relative_to(PACKAGE)
            saved.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            saved.write_bytes(content)
    try:
        for path, value in changed.items():
            path.write_text(value)
        built = subprocess.run(
            [
                "/bin/bash",
                "-lc",
                "source env.sh; colcon build --symlink-install --packages-select vacuum_sim",
            ],
            cwd=WS,
            text=True,
            stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
            stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
            timeout=180,
        )
        if built.returncode:
            raise RuntimeError(
                "Camera configuration build failed: " + built.stdout[-4000:]
            )
    except BaseException:
        for path, content in originals.items():
            if content is None:
                path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
            else:
                path.write_bytes(content)
        raise
    print("Camera target set to 60 FPS; direct driving view prepared.", flush=True)


def prepare():
    """Update view settings without changing the saved robot assembly."""

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Simulation-only adapter for Jazzy's unstamped teleop/Nav2 Twist messages.

Publishes only on receipt. The diff-drive controller enforces its 0.5 s timeout.
This module does not implement an emergency stop for a physical robot.
"""
import math
import rclpy
from geometry_msgs.msg import Twist, TwistStamped
from rclpy.node import Node


class TwistAdapter(Node):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__('simulation_twist_adapter')
        self.publisher = self.create_publisher(TwistStamped, '/diff_drive_controller/cmd_vel', 10)
        self.subscription = self.create_subscription(Twist, '/cmd_vel', self.on_twist, 10)

    def on_twist(self, message):
        outgoing = TwistStamped()
        outgoing.header.stamp = self.get_clock().now().to_msg()
        outgoing.header.frame_id = 'base_footprint'
        if math.isfinite(message.linear.x) and math.isfinite(message.angular.z):
            outgoing.twist.linear.x = max(-0.30, min(0.50, message.linear.x))
            outgoing.twist.angular.z = max(-1.2, min(1.2, message.angular.z))
        self.publisher.publish(outgoing)


def main():
    rclpy.init()
    node = TwistAdapter()
    try:
        rclpy.spin(node)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass
    finally:
        node.destroy_node()
        if rclpy.ok():
            rclpy.shutdown()


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

Open **Vacuum Lab.exe**. The dark launcher includes driving, mapping/navigation, the project file browser, a room preview and your hardware profile. **Drive now** opens the simulator, camera viewer and Alpha controller panel.

## Drive with the yoke

1. Center the yoke and release STOP.
2. Click **Arm drive** once.

The obstacle guard remains active. It allows reversing away from a front obstacle or moving forward away from a rear obstacle when that direction is clear.

The Alpha profile uses Y for speed, X for steering and button 3 for STOP. The dead zone is 5%. If pulling gives positive preview speed, pull back and click **Set pull = reverse**, then return to neutral. **Set neutral center** recalibrates axes. Save/load profiles preserve the optional button requirement; older profiles load without requiring a button.

**Keep drive armed when switching windows** starts enabled so you can select the camera or Gazebo while driving. Disable it to require panel focus. Changing bindings or focus behavior disarms drive. Status compares requested, guarded and actual speed and explains blocked movement.

Manual limits are **1.5 m/s forward**, **0.9 m/s reverse** and **2.4 rad/s turning**. Windows input and ROS command forwarding run at 50 Hz. Acceleration is 6 m/s²; odometry uses three samples at 60 Hz. Camera target remains 60 FPS at 320 × 240. Current performance and response measurements are in **modern-drive-validation.json**.

## Your robot and world

The model uses **two NEMA 17 motors beneath the chassis**, **two TB6600 drivers**, **Arduino Mega 2560**, **Orange Pi 5**, **RPLIDAR C1** and **7 cm diameter wheels**. **All project files** browses/searches the live Ubuntu workspace and hidden files, source, maps, logs, validation, rollback backups, installed ROS packages, original Windows files, Ubuntu disk/image and full backups. The first location contains files extracted from the EXE. Open files, reveal them in Explorer or copy their paths.

**Mapping + navigation** starts SLAM/Nav2 and RViz. Use **Nav2 Goal** in RViz to choose a destination. Autonomous navigation retains its 0.20 m/s planner limit. **Save current map** writes a unique map in `~/vacuum_ws/maps` while mapping runs. Switching workflows restarts the simulator and resets the current pose and live map; save first if needed.

**Stop lab** shuts down the launcher-owned simulation. Closing the main menu leaves the simulator running; closing the controller stops its commands. **Open robot code** connects VS Code to the workspace; **Ubuntu terminal** opens a shell.

The existing WSL distro is `VacuumRobot-24.04`, user `robot`, workspace `/home/robot/vacuum_ws`.
